_comment: MANIFEST-style expected-category fixture for the Pillar 2 (Shelf-Life Inference) corpus under testdata/python/shelf_life_examples.py and testdata/java/ShelfLifeExamples.java (see docs/SHELF_LIFE.md). Consumed by tests/golden/test_shelf_life_golden.py. expected_category: null means NO ShelfLifeFinding must be produced at all (genuinely no signal, never a silent generic_pii guess).

python.scenario: SHA256.new(aadhaar_bytes) -- the call argument itself names the aadhaar category (call_argument candidate kind)
SHA512.new(temp_cache_value) inside cache_temp_value() -- no candidate anywhere matches any category -- no finding at all

SHA3_256.new(record_bytes) inside CustomerRecord.hash_record() -- resolved via same-class dataclass fields aadhaar_number + account_number (model_field candidate kind); aadhaar wins the longest-shelf-life-wins tie-break over financial_account

java.scenario: MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256") inside hashAadhaarNumber() -- the enclosing method name names the aadhaar category (enclosing_function candidate kind)
MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-512") inside cacheTempValue() -- no candidate anywhere matches any category -- no finding at all

MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA3-256") inside CustomerRecord.hashRecord() -- resolved via same-class fields aadhaarNumber + accountNumber (model_field candidate kind); aadhaar wins the longest-shelf-life-wins tie-break over financial_account
